title: Add service-account-scoped RBAC mappings, KMS binding assertions, and compact audit headers
author: Lila Vasquez
description: Motivation: customers with strict least-privilege requirements requested a way to bind RBAC v2 roles directly to service accounts with region-aware KMS constraints while reducing audit overhead for high-throughput inference calls. This PR introduces a service-account-scoped RBAC mapper, KMS binding assertion middleware, and a compact audit header encoder to reduce telemetry size. Changes include: - RBAC: new policy translation layer (pkg/auth/rbac/v2/sa_mapper.go) that computes role mappings derived from service-account metadata and tenant claims, preserving existing role precedence semantics. Includes migration shim for legacy role mappings. - KMS: kms-binding-assertion middleware (infra/kms/assertion_proxy.go) that appends signed binding assertions when the tenant requests region-pin enforcement. Supports multi-provider keys and falls back to configured primary. - Audit: compact header encoder (internal/audit/compact_encoder.go) that compresses frequent audit fields into a base64-safe compact envelope with a version header. Runtime can opt-out via REDWOOD_AUDIT_COMPRESSION=false to preserve current logs. - Config: console flags and helm chart changes to enable toggles per-deployment (helm/redwood-private/templates/kms-proxy.yaml, values.yaml entries). - Tests & docs: unit + integration tests for mapper and assertion flow, plus a migration guide and rollout playbook (docs/security/sa-rbac-kms.md). Rollout plan: 1) Feature gate off by default on production clusters. 2) Canary enable for Dedicated tenants with low risk and expanded logging. 3) After 2 weeks of observability checks (audit integrity, latency, error-rates), promote to gradual rollout. Backwards compatibility: assertion middleware preserves legacy headers when tenant opt-in is missing. Audit encoder emits V1 header to allow decoders to fallback. Monitoring: dashboard widgets were added to console for assertion failure rate, audit envelope compression ratio, and mapper resolution time. Migration notes: operators must provide a KMS signing key for the assertion proxy and enable the SA mapping feature flag for tenant namespaces. Checklist: - [x] RBAC mapper implementation - [x] KMS assertion middleware + provider adapters - [x] Compact audit encoder + env toggle - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Helm + values entries - [x] Console feature flag UI excerpts

Tomás Muñoz: KMS assertion signing flow looks good but needs a stronger retry/backoff for transient KMS errors; also add metrics for signing latency.

release_notes: Introduce SA-scoped RBAC mappings, region-aware KMS binding assertions, and compact audit headers. Feature-gated and off by default. Operators must configure a KMS signing key and enable the feature flag for tenant namespaces. See docs/security/sa-rbac-kms.md for migration and rollout steps.
